A stronger lower back for pulling usually comes from a few basics, not a pile of extras. Back extensions or good mornings build the spinal erectors directly, rows with a braced, flat torso build the upper back that keeps you rigid off the floor, and Romanian deadlifts load the hamstrings and low back through a long range. Pause deadlifts or deficit pulls then build strength right where you need it. Pick one or two, keep the reps moderate, and give them a slot after your main pull rather than stacking all of them.

If you want, I can add one of those to your program. Tell me which one and which day.
